question.text: Exchange-traded derivatives are treated as non-speculative because:

answer.text: They are traded on recognized stock exchanges, making them eligible for non-speculative treatment even without physical delivery
All derivatives are non-speculative by default
Only options are non-speculative, not futures

explanation.text: The Logic: Eligible derivative transactions carried out on a recognized stock exchange are not deemed speculative, and exchange-traded currency derivative income/loss is treated as normal non-speculative business income even though delivery does not occur. The recognized-stock-exchange status is the operative condition. The Trap: Derivatives are not non-speculative by default; OTC derivatives without delivery can still be speculative. The RBI does not assign the speculative/non-speculative tag, and the rule does not discriminate between options and futures.
